title: Canonical derived-to-ordinary tensor comparison of module sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use all $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their symmetric monoidal tensor [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], and the K-flat derived tensor on $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Write $sF=F[0]$ for the degree-zero embedding. There is a canonical natural morphism
$$m_{F,G}:sF\otimes^{\mathbf L}sG\longrightarrow s(F\otimes G).$$
Its normalization is the augmentation of flat resolutions: for any nonpositive termwise-flat K-flat resolutions $P\to F[0]$ and $Q\to G[0]$, the representative of $m_{F,G}$ on $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$ is the tensor of the two augmentations followed by the unsigned identification $\operatorname{Tot}(F[0]\otimes G[0])=(F\otimes G)[0]$. The degree-zero unit comparison is the identity $\mathbf1_{D(\mathcal O_X)}=s\mathcal O_X$. These specified maps, rather than arbitrary maps with these endpoints, make $s$ a lax symmetric monoidal functor. Explicitly, with $\alpha^D,\sigma^D,\lambda^D,\rho^D$ the derived constraints and $\alpha,\tau,\lambda,\rho$ the ordinary constraints,
$$s(\alpha)\circ m_{F\otimes G,L}\circ(m_{F,G}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1)=m_{F,G\otimes L}\circ(1\otimes^{\mathbf L}m_{G,L})\circ\alpha^D,$$
$$s(\tau)\circ m_{F,G}=m_{G,F}\circ\sigma^D,$$
$$s(\lambda_F)\circ m_{\mathcal O_X,F}=\lambda^D_{sF},\qquad s(\rho_F)\circ m_{F,\mathcal O_X}=\rho^D_{sF}.$$
No flatness of $F,G,L$, quasi-coherence, or finiteness hypothesis is imposed; $m_{F,G}$ is a morphism and is not asserted to be invertible.

proof.text: Work on the small Zariski site of $X$, in a universe containing its opens and module sheaves. Abelian sheafification exists and is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], and a map of abelian presheaves becomes invertible after sheafification exactly when it is locally injective and locally surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective]. So the additive sheafification hypotheses of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] and of [lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints] hold. Apply that result to $R=\mathcal O_X$. Write $Q$ for localization of complexes and $\mu_{A,B}:QA\otimes^{\mathbf L}QB\to Q(A\otimes B)$ for its canonical lax tensorator. This is natural, obeys the lax associativity and unit laws, and preserves the Koszul braiding. When either factor is K-flat, $\mu$ is the inverse of the normalized total-tensor comparison. The fixed structure of [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] is this K-flat construction, with unit $Q(\mathcal O_X[0])$. Use its normalized unit identification throughout: the localization unit comparison is the identity under that identification, rather than an additional scalar automorphism.

proof.text: Let $tF=F[0]$ in complexes, and $s=Qt$. The direct-sum formula of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives a natural unsigned isomorphism $e_{F,G}:tF\otimes tG\xrightarrow{\sim}t(F\otimes G)$: only the $(0,0)$ summand is nonzero and all differentials vanish. These isomorphisms carry the native complex associator, braiding and unitors (those of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]) to the ordinary constraints of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Indeed [lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints] gives the native complex constraints on pure generators: the associator sends $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$, the braiding is $(-1)^{pq}$ times the swap on the $(p,q)$ summand, and the unitors send $a\otimes x$ and $x\otimes a$ to $ax$. The only nonzero triple summand is $(0,0,0)$, where the first formula is the ordinary associator; the braiding sign is $(-1)^{0\cdot0}=1$; the unit formulas on the only nonzero summand are the ordinary unitors. Pure generators detect maps out of these sheafified summands, so the equations hold as maps. Thus these checks are just identities on the indicated summands, with no resolution or flatness assertion.

proof.text:
Define $m_{F,G}=Q(e_{F,G})\circ\mu_{tF,tG}$. Naturality of $e$ and of the tensorator makes $m$ natural in both sheaves. For any resolutions $a:P\to tF$ and $b:T\to tG$ as in the statement, naturality gives
$$m_{F,G}\circ(Qa\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qb)=Q\bigl(e_{F,G}\circ(a\otimes b)\bigr)\circ\mu_{P,T}.$$
Here $Qa,Qb$ are isomorphisms by localization, and $\mu_{P,T}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]. Hence this equation is precisely the required representative on $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes T)$, under the normalized K-flat model comparison. It holds for every such pair, so also proves independence of the chosen pair. Neither $a\otimes b$ nor $m$ is claimed to be an isomorphism; nonflat $F,G$ are allowed.

proof.text:
For associativity, put $A=tF,B=tG,C=tL$. Expand the left side of the required equation using the definition of $m$. Move $Q(e_{F,G})$ through the next tensorator by its naturality. The resulting composite is
$$Q\bigl(t(\alpha)\circ e_{F\otimes G,L}\circ(e_{F,G}\otimes1)\bigr)\circ\mu_{A\otimes B,C}\circ(\mu_{A,B}\otimes^{\mathbf L}1).$$
Use the lax associativity law of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] to replace the last two tensorators by $\mu_{A,B\otimes C}\circ(1\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mu_{B,C})\circ\alpha^D$, together with $Q$ of the complex associator on the other side of the equality. Step 2 identifies the remaining complex composite with $e_{F,G\otimes L}\circ(1\otimes e_{G,L})$ after that associator. Naturality moves $Q(e_{G,L})$ back through $\mu$. The result is exactly $m_{F,G\otimes L}\circ(1\otimes^{\mathbf L}m_{G,L})\circ\alpha^D$. This uses the lax law on all complexes, and does not assume the intermediate sheaf $F\otimes G$ is flat.

proof.text:
For symmetry, step 2 gives $t(\tau)\circ e_{F,G}=e_{G,F}\circ\sigma^{\mathrm{complex}}_{tF,tG}$. To use braiding compatibility even when $tF,tG$ are not K-flat, choose termwise-flat K-flat replacements $P\to tF$, $T\to tG$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. On $(P,T)$, compatibility of the normalized comparison with the complex braiding, supplied by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], gives the braided equation for $\mu_{P,T}$ after inverting that comparison. Naturality of $\mu$, and of both braidings, identifies the equation for $(tF,tG)$ precomposed with $QP\otimes^{\mathbf L}QT\xrightarrow{\sim}sF\otimes^{\mathbf L}sG$ with this equation. Cancel that isomorphism. Thus
$$s(\tau)\circ m_{F,G}=Q(e_{G,F})\circ Q(\sigma^{\mathrm{complex}})\circ\mu_{tF,tG}=m_{G,F}\circ\sigma^D.$$
For the left unit, let $I=t\mathcal O_X$. Step 2 identifies $t(\lambda_F)\circ e_{\mathcal O_X,F}$ with the complex left unitor. The lax left-unit law therefore identifies $s(\lambda_F)\circ m_{\mathcal O_X,F}$ with $\lambda^D_{sF}$, since its extra unit-comparison factor is the identity in the normalization of step 1 and [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. The same calculation using the complex right unitor and the lax right-unit law gives $s(\rho_F)\circ m_{F,\mathcal O_X}=\rho^D_{sF}$. These are exactly the asserted symmetric lax monoidal equations for the maps normalized in step 3.
